_comment: Release-owned declaration of WHICH package-source revision an official
release is entitled to consume. Authority lives here, in the release repo,
never in whatever checkout the builder happens to encounter.
Before this file, provenance resolved R as the owning repo's HEAD: that
proves bytes are in git, but not WHICH revision a release may use. Checking
out an older packages commit would still have passed. Reproducible is not
the same as pinned.
One revision pins the whole metadata corpus. Individual .deb files are not
pinned separately - the git revision already provides an immutable
namespace, and the per-deb blob OID + sha256 emitted by the provenance gate
supply the finer-grained proof.
Release assembly materializes package bytes FROM this revision's git
objects. It does not read the sibling worktree and then check whether the
bytes happen to match. That distinction matters: the packages checkout may
legitimately carry unrelated in-progress work (it currently does), and that
work must be neither consumed by a release nor disturbed by one.
2026-08-16: this pin now also governs VALIDATION, not just release assembly.
CI checks globulario/packages out at exactly this revision before running
check-package-kinds and check-package-authority. Previously those gates ran
against whatever packages@main happened to be, so the same services commit
could pass one day and fail the next without changing - and a packages
change could turn services red with no services commit involved at all.
That is what happened on 2026-08-15: packages#17 removed 32 metadata
directories and every services PR went red on check-package-authority.
Bump it with `make bump-packages-pin` (or REV=<sha>), in its own commit,
so that adopting a new package corpus is a reviewable decision with a
diff - never a side effect of someone else pushing to packages.
